title: incident-bot: oncall runbook priority sampling and diagnostics heuristics
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improve runbook suggestion ranking by sampling on-call confirmations and adding heuristics to prioritize high-value diagnostics. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: On-call engineers reported noisy runbook suggestions during incidents where multiple SLOs fire. This PR introduces runbook priority sampling logic and a set of heuristics for incident-bot to score diagnostics and quicklinks so that on-call helpers surface the most relevant remediation steps. Changes include: prioritized sampling for runbook suggestions, SLO-weighted scoring, frequency-based de-duplication, and a small telemetry event to measure suggestion acceptance rate. The description below lists commits, changed areas, review discussions, CI summary, and merge details.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we add a brief note on why we choose reservoir sampling vs. top-k? Concerned about starvation for low-frequency runbooks.
Maya Chen: Response: reservoir sampling preserves diversity and avoids repeatedly surfacing the same high-popularity runbooks; added a parameter to control bias toward higher scores.
Priya Nair: Please ensure telemetry doesn't include any PII or incident-specific identifiers. Also add an opt-out flag for telemetry in private deployments.
Maya Chen: Addressed: telemetry emits only hashed ids and we added "opt_out_telemetry" config with tests. See telemetry/events.yaml change.
Carlos Ramirez: Approving pending small test fix for the dedupe case when titles differ but URLs match.
Maya Chen: Fixed dedupe to normalize URLs and added unit test to cover title variation.

qa_notes: Manual QA: Simulated incident with two overlapping SLOs, verified suggestions show SLO-weighted ranking and duplicates collapsed.
Performance: CPU overhead on suggestion path < 3% p50 in canary region; sampling window parameter default tuned to keep latency < 30ms.
Privacy: telemetry uses hashed identifiers; config flag added for private deployment opt-out.
